edits.say: Leave a long tail. Make a loop near the end of the rope, take the tail under and around the standing rope, then push it down through the loop, the last opening. You should have a loose figure-eight with the standing rope hanging down on the left and the long tail coming out on the right.
placements: white rope with green flecks, working end → loop formed, tail taken under and around the standing rope, then down through the first loop (final opening), giving a loose figure-eight held horizontally in front of the trunk
standing rope → hanging down out of the left side of the loose figure-eight
long tail → coming out of the right side of the loose figure-eight, held in the right hand

why: 0:06-0:10 he measures off a LONG tail; 0:12 and 0:16 show the UNDER captions and 0:18 shows THROUGH THE FINAL OPENING. In the end frame (0:20) the standing rope hangs down on the left and the tail leaves on the right, not hanging down on the left as the current text says.
0:24-0:28 the knot is held left of the trunk while the tail goes up, around behind the trunk and comes down on the right side (end frame).

0:30 RETRACE: the tail tip enters the knot next to its own exit; 0:34 OTHER DIRECTION; 0:36-0:42 he threads it through; 0:44 the doubled knot is done with the tail coming out the bottom beside the standing rope.
0:46-0:50 he dresses the doubled strands with his fingers, with the captions 3 SETS OF PARALLEL and EACH SIDE.
0:52 and 1:02-1:04 he pulls the standing rope and tail down-left against the loop around the trunk; 0:54-1:00 show the tight knot at the left of the trunk.
The stopper is already tied by 1:08 (the tying itself is cut out between 1:06 and 1:08); 1:12 shows the DOUBLE OVERHAND STOPPER caption and 1:14-1:20 show it snug below the main knot.
